evals.prompt: Give me a health report on data sources before I run inference.
evals.expected_output: Staleness against per-type thresholds from the table, not a flat threshold; verifies source list against real files.
expectations: Queries source freshness (resolved_series / source_catalog or the system health endpoint) rather than assuming
Applies per-source-type thresholds (real-time >1h, daily >36h, weekly >8d, monthly >35d, high-frequency alt-data >6h) rather than a single cutoff
Reports OK/WARNING/CRITICAL by source and a summary count
Verifies that endpoints and ingestion file paths the skill names actually exist before relying on them (for example /api/health/sources and ingestion/market/*) and reports any that do not

evals.prompt: Check which API keys are configured and tell me what will break silently.
evals.expected_output: FRED_API_KEY is the only one validated at startup; others fail silently.
expectations: States FRED_API_KEY is the only key validated at startup (config.py) and is required
Lists KOSIS, COMTRADE, JQUANTS, USDA, NOAA, EIA keys as silent-failure keys (401 / empty results / rate limits)
Checks presence of keys via config values (booleans) and never prints the key values themselves
Recommends warning-level logging for missing optional keys

evals.prompt: Model predictions look off. I think a series has NaNs that got silently converted. How do I audit it?
evals.expected_output: ATTENTION #13/#14 NaN handling audit and graceful degradation.
expectations: Treats silent NaN conversion as a candidate cause and audits the specific series over a recent window (for example 7 days)
Compares NaN handling across ingestion modules for inconsistency
Recommends flagging or failing on NaN rather than silently coercing to 0 or forward-filling without a log
Checks data freshness for the affected series as a competing explanation
